analysis.investment_thesis: AEQUS has negative EBIT (~-17 Cr on -1.84% operating margin vs. 925 Cr revenue), making the Magic Formula entirely inapplicable — you cannot buy earnings you don't have. The stock trades at 288x EV/EBITDA and 12.85x P/B with no path to near-term profitability, making it one of the most overvalued names I've seen.
key_strengths: High gross margin of 56% suggests underlying product economics could work if overhead is controlled
59% promoter holding indicates founder-led conviction and skin in the game
Large CWIP (INR 395 Cr) signals capacity build-out that could drive future revenue scale
key_risks: Negative EBIT (-1.84% operating margin) means Magic Formula earnings yield is negative — uninvestable by my framework
Free cash flow deeply negative (-239 Cr in FY25) while capex accelerates to 265 Cr with no earnings to fund it
EV/EBITDA of 288x and Forward P/E of 1,140x represent extreme valuation with zero margin of safety
red_flags: EBIT is negative — Magic Formula cannot function; earnings yield < 0%
ROCE of 1.11% is catastrophically below my 12% minimum threshold
Net profit worsened dramatically from -14 Cr (FY24) to -102 Cr (FY25) despite similar revenues
Revenue actually declined from 965 Cr to 925 Cr year-over-year — growth thesis is not executing
Debt/Equity of 1.08 with negative retained earnings history (reserves only just turned positive at 135 Cr)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula requires two things: high earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and high return on capital. AEQUS fails both catastrophically. With an operating margin of -1.84% on INR 925 Cr revenue, EBIT is approximately -17 Cr. Against an enterprise value of ~11,926 Cr (market cap 11,202 + debt 785 - cash 61), the earnings yield is deeply negative. ROCE of 1.11% is essentially zero — the business is destroying capital, not compounding it. My formula demands a minimum 12% earnings yield AND 20%+ ROIC; AEQUS delivers neither.

The business narrative is an industrial cluster/contract manufacturing story still in heavy investment mode, which explains the 395 Cr CWIP and accelerating capex of 265 Cr in FY25. But the numbers show a deteriorating trajectory: net losses widened from -14 Cr to -102 Cr, free cash flow hit -239 Cr, and revenue actually shrank. The 56% gross margin is intriguing and suggests unit economics might work eventually — but "eventually" is not a price I can pay at 288x EV/EBITDA. There is no margin of safety here whatsoever.
